title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 29 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 29.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 29, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: He repaired the doors of the house of the LORD
He gathered the priests and Levites
He made a covenant with the LORD God of Israel
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:1.

questions.question: How old was Hezekiah when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah began to reign when he was 25 years old, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:1.

questions.question: For how many years did Hezekiah reign in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah reigned for 29 years in Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:1.

questions.question: Who was Hezekiah's mother?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's mother's name was Abijah, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:1.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do in the first month of his reign?
options: Opened the doors of the house of the LORD
Made a covenant with the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Opened the doors of the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: In the first year of his reign, in the first month, Hezekiah opened the doors of the house of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:3.

questions.question: What command did Hezekiah give to the Levites?
options: Repair the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Hezekiah commanded the Levites to sanctify themselves, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:5.

questions.question: What was the state of the holy place before Hezekiah's reforms?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah stated that they needed to carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place, indicating it was unclean, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:5.

questions.question: What had the fathers done that was evil in the eyes of the LORD?
options: Closed the doors of the temple
questions.explanation: The fathers have trespassed and forsaken the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:6.

questions.question: What happened to Judah and Jerusalem due to their actions?
options: They faced the wrath of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They faced the wrath of the LORD
questions.explanation: The wrath of the LORD was upon Judah and Jerusalem because of their actions, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:8.

questions.question: What does Hezekiah want to do to turn away the LORD's fierce wrath?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah expresses his intention to make a covenant with the LORD God of Israel to turn away His fierce wrath, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:10.

questions.question: What were the Levites chosen to do?
questions.explanation: The LORD hath chosen the Levites to stand before Him and serve Him, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:11.

questions.question: Did Mahath and Joel belong to the Kohathites?
questions.explanation: Mahath the son of Amasai and Joel the son of Azariah were of the sons of the Kohathites, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:12.

questions.question: Did Hezekiah's reforms occur in the first year of his reign?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah opened the doors of the house of the LORD in the first year of his reign, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:3.

questions.question: The doors of the porch were left open during Hezekiah's reign.
questions.explanation: The text states that they had shut up the doors of the porch, as seen in 2 Chronicles 29:7.

questions.question: Hezekiah's mother was the daughter of Moses.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's mother was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah, not Moses, as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:1.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 29 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Elizaphan mentioned in 2 Chronicles 29:13?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states the sons of Elizaphan are Shimri and Jeiel (2 Chronicles 29:13).

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 29:15 promise will happen if someone sanctifies themselves as commanded in 2 Chronicles 29:5?
options: They will cleanse the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They will cleanse the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Sanctifying oneself leads to the cleansing of the house of the LORD as commanded (2 Chronicles 29:15).

questions.question: What did the priests do with the uncleanness they found in the temple according to 2 Chronicles 29:16?
options: They brought it into the court
questions.correctAnswer: They brought it into the court
questions.explanation: The priests brought out all the uncleanness into the court of the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:16).

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 29:17, when did they begin to sanctify the house of the LORD?
options: On the first day of the first month
On the eighth day of the month
On the sixteenth day of the month
On the last day of the month
questions.correctAnswer: On the first day of the first month
questions.explanation: They began to sanctify on the first day of the first month (2 Chronicles 29:17).

questions.question: What was the purpose of the offerings brought by Hezekiah according to 2 Chronicles 29:21?
options: For the kingdom and the sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: For the kingdom and the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Hezekiah commanded the offerings for the kingdom and the sanctuary (2 Chronicles 29:21).

questions.question: What did the priests do with the blood of the offerings in 2 Chronicles 29:22?
questions.explanation: The priests sprinkled the blood on the altar after killing the offerings (2 Chronicles 29:22).

questions.question: What did they do to make atonement for all Israel according to 2 Chronicles 29:24?
questions.explanation: They made reconciliation with the blood upon the altar to make atonement for all Israel (2 Chronicles 29:24).

questions.question: How long did it take to sanctify the house of the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 29:17?
questions.explanation: They sanctified the house of the LORD in eight days (2 Chronicles 29:17).

questions.question: What command did Hezekiah give regarding the offerings in 2 Chronicles 29:21?
options: To offer them on the altar
To give them to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: To offer them on the altar
questions.explanation: Hezekiah commanded the priests to offer the offerings on the altar (2 Chronicles 29:21).

questions.question: Why was the wrath of the LORD upon Judah and Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 29:8?
questions.explanation: The wrath of the LORD was upon them because they had forsaken Him (2 Chronicles 29:8).

questions.question: What did Hezekiah want to do to turn away the fierce wrath of the LORD as stated in 2 Chronicles 29:10?
options: Make a covenant with the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Make a covenant with the LORD
questions.explanation: Hezekiah expressed a desire to make a covenant with the LORD to turn away His wrath (2 Chronicles 29:10).

questions.question: The Levites were chosen to stand before the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 29:11. What were they to do?
questions.explanation: The Levites were chosen to stand before the LORD to serve Him and burn incense (2 Chronicles 29:11).

questions.question: The priests received the blood of the bullocks according to 2 Chronicles 29:22. True or False?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the priests received the blood of the bullocks to sprinkle it on the altar (2 Chronicles 29:22).

questions.question: The sons of Heman mentioned in 2 Chronicles 29:14 were Jehiel and Shimei. True or False?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the sons of Heman were indeed Jehiel and Shimei (2 Chronicles 29:14).

questions.question: Hezekiah reigned for thirty-five years in Jerusalem. True or False?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 29:1).

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 29.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 29:25, which instruments did Hezekiah set the Levites to play in the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 29:25 states that Hezekiah set the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, psalteries, and harps according to the commandment of David and the prophets.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 29:26, who stood with the instruments of David, and who stood with the trumpets?
options: Levites with instruments, priests with trumpets
Priests with instruments, Levites with trumpets
Levites with trumpets, priests with harps
Singers with instruments, priests with cymbals
questions.correctAnswer: Levites with instruments, priests with trumpets
questions.explanation: Verse 26 clearly says the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

questions.question: What event began simultaneously with the burnt offering according to 2 Chronicles 29:27?
options: The song of the LORD with trumpets and instruments
questions.correctAnswer: The song of the LORD with trumpets and instruments
questions.explanation: Verse 27 states that when the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD began also with trumpets and the instruments ordained by David.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 29:28, how long did the singing and trumpeting continue?
options: Until the burnt offering was finished
Until the king gave the signal
questions.correctAnswer: Until the burnt offering was finished
questions.explanation: Verse 28 says all continued—the singers sang and trumpeters sounded—until the burnt offering was finished.

questions.question: Who bowed and worshipped after the burnt offering was completed as described in 2 Chronicles 29:29?
options: The king and all present with him
questions.correctAnswer: The king and all present with him
questions.explanation: Verse 29 specifies that after offering, the king and all present bowed themselves and worshipped.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 29:30, whose words did the Levites sing praises with?
questions.explanation: Verse 30 states the Levites sang praise with the words of David and of Asaph the seer.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'kodesh' in 2 Chronicles 29:5 most accurately mean?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 29:5, the Hebrew word 'kodesh' is used for sanctify or consecrate, indicating setting apart for holy use.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in 2 Chronicles 29:25-30, with the Levites and priests playing different instruments in an orchestrated worship?
questions.explanation: The passage frames the worship activities with specific instruments and roles, creating an inclusio that brackets the worship event.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of consecrated musical worship found in 2 Chronicles 29:25-30?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:19 encourages speaking to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, echoing the consecrated musical worship of 2 Chronicles 29:25-30.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to Hezekiah's restoration of temple worship in 2 Chronicles 29:1-36?
questions.explanation: Ezra 3:10-13 describes the restoration of temple worship after exile, similar to Hezekiah’s restoration in 2 Chronicles 29.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the setting of Levites with musical instruments in 2 Chronicles 29:25?
options: The atonement with the sin offering for all Israel
The gathering of the rulers of the city
questions.correctAnswer: The atonement with the sin offering for all Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 29:24, just before verse 25, describes the atonement made by the sin offering for all Israel, preceding the musical worship setup.

questions.question: What typological significance can be drawn from the Levites helping priests to flay burnt offerings in 2 Chronicles 29:34?
options: It foreshadows the New Testament priesthood being supported by the church body
It represents the rejection of Levitical law
It symbolizes the division between priests and Levites
It indicates the end of temple sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the New Testament priesthood being supported by the church body
questions.explanation: Verse 34 shows Levites assisting priests, typologically pointing to the New Testament where all believers support the priestly ministry (1 Peter 2:9).

questions.question: Which parallelism literary device is evident in 2 Chronicles 29:28 describing the simultaneous actions of the congregation, singers, and trumpeters?
questions.explanation: Verse 28 shows synthetic parallelism where the actions build upon each other (worship, singing, trumpeting) to complete the scene.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 29:36, Hezekiah and the people rejoiced because God had prepared them suddenly.
questions.explanation: Verse 36 explicitly states Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced because God had prepared the people and the thing was done suddenly.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Chronicles 29:32 records that the congregation brought only ten bullocks for burnt offerings.
questions.explanation: Verse 32 states the congregation brought seventy (threescore and ten) bullocks, not ten, along with other animals for burnt offerings.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 29 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 29 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 29:2 teach about human sin and divine approval?
options: Human righteousness is measured by conformity to David’s example before God
God approves only sacrifices without regard to moral behavior
Human kingship guarantees divine approval regardless of actions
Only temple rituals determine divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Human righteousness is measured by conformity to David’s example before God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 29:2 states Hezekiah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD according to all that David his father had done, teaching that divine approval is linked to righteous behavior modeled after David.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in 2 Chronicles 29:5?
options: Sanctification requires deliberate separation and cleansing from defilement
Sanctification is automatic for priests and Levites
Sanctification is solely a communal act without individual responsibility
Sanctification is only about external rituals without internal change
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification requires deliberate separation and cleansing from defilement
questions.explanation: Verse 5 exhorts the Levites to sanctify themselves and the house of the LORD, indicating sanctification involves intentional separation and cleansing from filthiness.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenant renewal is emphasized in 2 Chronicles 29:10?
options: Covenant renewal is a means to avert God's fierce wrath through repentance
Covenant renewal nullifies previous disobedience without repentance
Covenant renewal depends on political alliances and military strength
Covenant renewal is only a symbolic gesture without real effect
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant renewal is a means to avert God's fierce wrath through repentance
questions.explanation: Hezekiah expresses a desire to make a covenant with the LORD so that His fierce wrath may turn away, showing covenant renewal seeks God's mercy through repentance (verse 10).

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 29:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 speaks of the wrath of the LORD being upon Judah and Jerusalem due to their sin, demonstrating God's attribute of righteous wrath.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly shown in 2 Chronicles 29:36?
questions.explanation: Verse 36 notes God had prepared the people suddenly, indicating His providential care and orchestration in the events.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 29:3–4 connect to the theme of temple restoration seen elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures the post-exilic temple rebuilding emphasizing renewed worship
It contradicts the prophetic calls for destruction of the temple
It highlights the permanent rejection of temple worship in favor of synagogues
It shows that temple worship was irrelevant after David’s reign
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the post-exilic temple rebuilding emphasizing renewed worship
questions.explanation: Hezekiah’s opening and repairing the temple doors (29:3–4) anticipates the post-exilic restoration under Ezra and Nehemiah, reinforcing themes of renewed dedication to God's house.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 2 Chronicles 29:21–24 have with the atonement in the New Testament?
options: The sin offerings for the kingdom prefigure Christ’s atoning sacrifice for all Israel
The animal sacrifices replace Christ’s sacrifice in the New Testament
The offerings demonstrate the sufficiency of works apart from grace
The atonement rituals were purely symbolic with no future fulfillment
questions.correctAnswer: The sin offerings for the kingdom prefigure Christ’s atoning sacrifice for all Israel
questions.explanation: The sin offerings made for the kingdom and sanctuary anticipate the ultimate atonement by Christ, who offers reconciliation for all Israel (29:21–24).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 29:15 and 29:16 teach about sanctification and cleansing?
options: Sanctification involves both the consecration of persons and the removal of impurity from sacred spaces
Sanctification is purely inward and does not affect physical surroundings
Only the Levites are required to sanctify themselves without cleansing the temple
Cleansing the temple is sufficient without personal sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves both the consecration of persons and the removal of impurity from sacred spaces
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 16 show the Levites sanctifying themselves and cleansing the temple of uncleanness, teaching sanctification includes personal holiness and purification of the holy place.

questions.question: What doctrine about worship and covenant faithfulness is taught by comparing 2 Chronicles 29:25 and 29:30?
options: Worship with music and praise according to divine ordinance reflects covenant faithfulness
Worship music is optional and unrelated to covenant obedience
Praise should be silent and not involve musical instruments
Covenant faithfulness excludes liturgical worship expressions
questions.correctAnswer: Worship with music and praise according to divine ordinance reflects covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 25 and 30 show Levites playing instruments and singing praises by commandment of the LORD, linking ordered worship to covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by synthesizing 2 Chronicles 29:31 and 29:32 about freewill offerings and corporate worship?
options: True worship includes voluntary, free-hearted offerings alongside prescribed sacrifices
Only mandatory sacrifices contribute to genuine worship
Freewill offerings undermine the authority of the priesthood
Corporate worship excludes individual voluntary contributions
questions.correctAnswer: True worship includes voluntary, free-hearted offerings alongside prescribed sacrifices
questions.explanation: Verse 31 invites the congregation to bring sacrifices and thank offerings with a free heart; verse 32 notes the abundance of burnt offerings, showing worship blends obligatory and voluntary elements.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Chronicles 29:11–14 shows a forced religious conformity lacking genuine holiness. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The Levites voluntarily sanctified themselves as a genuine response to divine calling
The Levites were coerced into sanctification by the king’s political power
Sanctification was a superficial act without internal commitment
Only a select few Levites sanctified themselves while others refused
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites voluntarily sanctified themselves as a genuine response to divine calling
questions.explanation: Verses 11–14 describe the Levites rising and sanctifying themselves according to the king’s command and the word of the LORD, indicating willing and heartfelt obedience.

questions.question: What doctrine about priestly service and Levite cooperation is taught in 2 Chronicles 29:34?
options: Levites assisted priests because of their greater zeal for sanctification
Levites were inferior and only helped due to priestly weakness
Priests and Levites operated independently without mutual aid
Only priests were responsible for temple rituals
questions.correctAnswer: Levites assisted priests because of their greater zeal for sanctification
questions.explanation: Verse 34 explains that Levites helped because they were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests, showing cooperation in temple service.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 2 Chronicles 29:24 by the king’s command for atonement for all Israel?
questions.explanation: The king’s command for sin offerings to make reconciliation for all Israel shows God’s mercy extended through atonement (verse 24).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared for in 2 Chronicles 29:20–23 by the offering of multiple sin offerings for the nation?
options: The need for a perfect and sufficient sacrifice for national sin
The sufficiency of animal sacrifices to permanently remove sin
The rejection of sacrificial atonement in Israel’s future
The elimination of priestly mediation in worship
questions.correctAnswer: The need for a perfect and sufficient sacrifice for national sin
questions.explanation: The multiple sin offerings foreshadow the ultimate perfect sacrifice needed for true atonement, which points toward Christ’s sacrifice.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 29:18–19 teach about the restoration of worship and the consequences of prior apostasy?
options: Restoration includes reclaiming and sanctifying vessels cast away due to former transgression
Once cast away, sacred vessels are permanently defiled and unusable
Apostasy has no impact on worship practices or sacred items
Worship restoration can occur without attention to past sins
questions.correctAnswer: Restoration includes reclaiming and sanctifying vessels cast away due to former transgression
questions.explanation: Verses 18–19 describe how vessels discarded by King Ahaz’s sinful reign were prepared and sanctified again, illustrating restoration after apostasy.
